back: Forest-wide: Schema Master, Domain Naming Master. Per domain: RID Master, PDC Emulator, Infrastructure Master. Keyword: two and three.
Transfer is graceful with the holder online. Seize is forcible — and a seized holder must never return to the network. Keyword: never bring it back.
Time authority, urgent password changes, lockout processing. Its loss shows up as authentication oddities. Keyword: felt first.
Nothing is cached by default, so a branch that must authenticate during a WAN outage needs accounts added deliberately. Keyword: opt in.
On a trust, requires an explicit allowed-to-authenticate permission per resource instead of trusting everyone. Keyword: per resource.

front: Subnet not associated with a site
back: Clients authenticate across the WAN to whatever controller answers — the classic slow branch logon. Keyword: map the subnet.
The KDS root key must exist in the forest before any group managed service account can be created. Keyword: root key first.
Standalone works on one machine; group managed works across many, which is what a farm or cluster needs. Keyword: one vs many.
Local, site, domain, then OU top down. Last writer wins. Keyword: LSDOU.
Block Inheritance stops higher policies — except an Enforced link, which still applies. Keyword: Enforced always wins.
A policy setting is enforced and reverts when it stops applying. A preference is written once and stays. Keyword: enforced vs set.
Credentials used to reach the first machine cannot pass to a second. Fix with resource-based constrained delegation, not CredSSP. Keyword: second hop fails.
Role capability plus session configuration; the session runs as a temporary virtual account the user never holds. Keyword: restart a service without being admin.
Policy, Defender for Servers, Monitor, extensions, and Update Manager all require the server to be projected into Azure first. Keyword: Arc first.
Assesses and deploys updates across Azure and Arc machines with maintenance configurations. Replaced Automation Update Management. Keyword: the current tool.
Audits and enforces settings inside the OS, so a baseline is held rather than applied once. Keyword: stops drift.
Azure Automation runbooks authenticate with a managed identity rather than a stored credential. Keyword: no stored secret.
UEFI boot, secure boot, virtual TPM, required for shielded VMs. Generation cannot be changed after creation. Keyword: choose at creation.
Unsuitable for workloads that manage their own memory, such as SQL Server — use a fixed assignment. Keyword: not for databases.
Production uses the guest's backup infrastructure for an application-consistent point. Standard captures memory and is unsafe for a DC. Keyword: production is the default.
Manages a guest through the hypervisor with no network path — the answer when guest networking is broken. Keyword: no network needed.
Replica is disaster recovery with bounded data loss. A cluster is high availability with shared storage and none. Keyword: RPO vs continuous.
Set spreads across fault and update domains in one datacentre. Zones spread across physically separate datacentres. Keyword: zones are stronger.
By the disk and by the VM size — a fast disk on a small VM still performs badly. Keyword: both limits apply.
Multi-master updates, directory replication, and secure dynamic updates. Preferred wherever the directory exists. Keyword: secure dynamic update.
Forwards only queries for a named domain — how hybrid resolves an Azure private zone or a partner namespace. Keyword: per domain.
Authenticity and integrity of the answer — not confidentiality. Keyword: signed, not encrypted.
A DHCP server in a domain must be authorised in AD before it serves leases. First thing to check. Keyword: authorise it.

front: Load balance vs hot standby failover
back: Load balance shares a scope by percentage between two servers. Hot standby designates active and reserve. Keyword: both active, or one waiting.
The most specific level wins — reservation over scope over server. Keyword: specific beats general.
Share-level Azure RBAC for SMB access plus NTFS permissions inside. Both must be right. Keyword: two layers.
Keeps hot files local and replaces cold ones with pointers, governed by free-space and date policies. Namespace stays intact. Keyword: pointers, not deletions.
Disable DFS Replication on a folder before enabling File Sync — two replication engines on one directory conflict. Keyword: one engine only.
The most restrictive combination of share and NTFS permissions — which is why share is usually Everyone Full Control. Keyword: most restrictive wins.
Hides items a user cannot read. Changes visibility, not permission. Keyword: hide, not deny.
Tunnels SMB inside QUIC over UDP 443, so a file server is reachable from the internet without a VPN. Keyword: no VPN.
It replicates faithfully — including deletion and corruption. Keyword: replicates mistakes too.
Escrow to AD or Entra ID; an unescrowed recovery key means an unrecoverable volume. Keyword: escrow or lose it.
Virtualisation-based isolation of secrets — the specific defence against pass-the-hash. Keyword: secrets out of reach.
A unique rotating local administrator password per machine, stored in AD or Entra. Stops lateral movement from one shared password. Keyword: no shared local password.
Disables weak authentication for members — no NTLM, no delegation, short tickets. Not for service accounts. Keyword: breaks services.
Password settings objects applied by precedence, so administrators can be held to stricter rules without a separate domain. Keyword: per group.
Separate from a firewall rule; establishes authenticated IPsec between machines. Combine for server isolation. Keyword: authenticate, don't just allow.
Run in audit mode before enforcement, or a policy blocks legitimate software on day one. Keyword: audit then enforce.
A counter value means little without something to compare it against — record data collector sets before problems appear. Keyword: measure early.
Better evidence of CPU saturation than processor time alone. Keyword: queue, not percentage.
Authentication fails beyond the permitted skew, default five minutes — and the error says authentication, not time. Keyword: check the clock.
Restores a deleted object with attributes and group memberships. Once enabled it cannot be disabled. Keyword: one-way switch.
Appear when a controller reconnects after being offline longer than the tombstone lifetime. Keyword: too long offline.
Repair with Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair rather than rejoining the domain. Keyword: repair, don't rejoin.
